file.@1: Chapter 1: The Tower-In-The-Middle-Of-The-StreetExcited: this is how Igor was. During his whole life, he had heard about the Tower-In-The-Middle-Of-The-Street, a famous building in the City-Of-Ravines, a scenery for many fabulous stories. Everyone wanted to go there, and now it was his turn. Tomorrow would be the big day!

file.@1: His sister was going to the City-Of-Ravines the next morning to visit someone (Igor didn't really care about who it was). Do you know where? Right: at the Tower-In-The-Middle-Of-The-Street! Igor asked if he could go with her to fulfill his dream. After all, he was already 15 years old and knew little, almost nothing, about the City-Of-Ravines. By following his sister, who knew the city pretty well, everything would be easier.So, they went there!

file.@1: If you were checking out Igor’s reactions as he approached the tower, you'd see some fixed, watchful eyes, and perhaps would also notice an unusual glint coming from them. Everything was there: the Tower-In-The-Middle-Of-The-Street, ancient, all-powerful, taking its place in the world. The Cathedral-That-Is-Not, with its own history and its own admirers, was just next door, crowded with the Monks-That-Are and the Monks-That-Once-Were, who were constantly coming in and out, saying their prayers, ringing their bells...

file.@1:
Igor stood still for some time, watching everything. He was thrilled. Before entering, he had already realized that the stories told about that place, even being epic, were nothing before the majesty of the famous tower.

Inside the building, everything was very confusing. The Tower-In-The-Middle-Of-The-Street was a mix of homes, shops and everything else imaginable. There were several entrances, and there were people, lots of people, moving hastily from side to side all the time.

file.@1:
Knowing he was at the right place made Igor's heart pound in his chest.

He and his sister went towards the elevators. They were very ancient and allowed the boy to see the floors going past behind bars. The elevator doors were meant to be open manually when someone wanted to enter or leave. Frightened, some people even decided to make their way back down through the stairs, from time to time, because of the bad experience with the elevator.

When they reached the floor they were heading to – a very high one – and were about to knock on the apartment door of Who-Knows-Who-It-Is, Igor told his sister:
– Sis', I will explore the building, OK? I think your conversation here will not interest me. So, I'm going down through the stairs, in order to check floor by floor. I heard that the first ones are the most interesting... Can I do it?

file.@1:
He didn't really wait for an answer; the boy flew to the stairs and started exploring everywhere as soon as he could.

But he did not go down as fast as it would be expected. No... he wanted to explore the place! He went down checking the doors and all spots, like a small child does when left in a new place. He wanted to see everything, know everything. Offices, cabinets, corridors... Every open door was a big temptation for Igor’s curiosity.

file.@1: The boy's excitement was really great, and so were the surprises he found on his way down. Unexpected sounds, like a symphony of cats meowing or a large waterfall, made him look everywhere, sometimes finding the source, others not. These things were just making him become more and more curious and his imagination was traveling wild. There were strange things in all places, such as “a group of ladies elegantly dressed for a prom in the 1920s, hurried by being very, very late”, thought Igor when he saw them.

file.@1: From surprise to surprise, Igor finally reached the fourth floor. The road had been long, but he was not tired. He had descended a lot, and was almost at the end of his adventure, heading to the stairs which led to the third floor. At that moment, a strange figure, coming from who knows where, held him tightly by the arm. It was a man at about 60 years of age, with an unkempt appearance, even smelling bad. His eyes were not fixing on anything for some time, what reinforced the idea of insanity. Igor was distressed and unresponsive for a moment, but soon recovered himself. That was when the man said loudly:

file.@1:
– You can go down, you do not have the key.

What did he mean by that? Igor glanced at the stairs in doubt for a second, but when he looked for the strange man, he was not there anymore. What was that? Where could that crazy man have gone? With fear of finding the odd creature again, and deriving a little pleasure from having lived one of those situations that surely would become another story of the Tower-In-The-Middle-Of-The-Street, he hastened toward the stairs.
